enonce.texte:
Identify whether each question is open or closed.

Closed questions can be answered with 'yes' or 'no'. Open questions require more information.

questions.texte: Do you like music?
questions.reponse: Closed

questions.texte: What kind of music do you like?
questions.reponse: Open

questions.texte: Did you watch the movie yesterday?
questions.reponse: Closed

questions.texte: Why did you choose to study English?
questions.reponse: Open

questions.texte: Are you a student?
questions.reponse: Closed

intitule: Exercise 2: Creating Open and Closed Questions

enonce.texte:
Transform the following statements into questions.

For each statement, create one open question and one closed question.

questions.texte: You have a job interview tomorrow.
questions.reponse: Closed: Do you have a job interview tomorrow? / Open: Why do you have a job interview tomorrow?

sousQuestions.reponse: Do you have a job interview tomorrow?
Why do you have a job interview tomorrow?

questions.texte: You are planning a trip to Paris.
questions.reponse: Closed: Are you planning a trip to Paris? / Open: Where are you planning to go?

sousQuestions.reponse: Are you planning a trip to Paris?
Where are you planning to go?

questions.texte: She works in a hospital.
questions.reponse: Closed: Does she work in a hospital? / Open: Where does she work?

sousQuestions.reponse: Does she work in a hospital?

enonce.texte:
Read the following situations and respond spontaneously.

Imagine you are in a conversation. Give a natural and appropriate response.

questions.texte: Your friend says: 'I just got a new job!'
questions.reponse: Congratulations! That's great news!

questions.texte: Your friend says: 'I had a terrible day at work.'
questions.reponse: I'm sorry to hear that. What happened?

questions.texte: Your friend says: 'I'm planning to travel to Japan next year.'
questions.reponse: That sounds exciting! When are you going?

questions.texte: What do you do for a living?
questions.reponse: Asking about someone's job

questions.texte: What's your favorite way to relax?
questions.reponse: Asking about hobbies/leisure

questions.texte: Have you seen any good movies lately?
questions.reponse: Asking about entertainment

questions.texte: Where are you from originally?
questions.reponse: Asking about nationality/origin

enonce.texte:
You are going to have a 10-minute conversation with a partner.

Choose one of the following topics and talk about it for at least 10 minutes. Ask open and closed questions. Respond spontaneously.

Topics:

  • Describe your ideal holiday
  • Talk about your favorite movie and why you like it
  • Discuss your future career plans
  • Share your opinion on social media

Write a summary of the conversation after you finish.

questions.texte: Write a summary of the conversation. Include the questions you asked and the answers you received.
questions.reponse: Example: I talked to my partner about their ideal holiday. I asked: 'What is your ideal holiday?' They said they would like to go to the beach. I asked: 'What do you like about the beach?' They said they like swimming and relaxing. I also asked: 'Have you ever been to a beach holiday?' They said yes, they went to the beach last year. I then shared my opinion and we discussed the best beaches in Cameroon.

enonce.texte: Choose the most appropriate response for each situation.

questions.texte: Your friend: 'I just got a promotion!'
questions.reponse: Wow, congratulations! That's wonderful!

questions.texte: Your friend: 'I feel really stressed lately.'
questions.reponse: I understand. Maybe you should take a break.

sousQuestions.reponse: I understand. Maybe you should take a break.

questions.texte: Your friend: 'I think we should study together.'
questions.reponse: That's a great idea! When can we start?

sousQuestions.reponse: That's a great idea! When can we start?

intitule: Exercise 7: Asking for Opinions and Expanding Ideas

enonce.texte:
Read the paragraph below. Then, ask three questions to get more information about the person's opinion.

Paragraph: 'I love living in the city because there are many opportunities. However, I don't like the traffic and noise. I prefer quiet places to relax.'

questions.texte: What opportunities do you like most about living in the city?
questions.reponse: The person might answer: 'I like the job opportunities and the cultural events.'

questions.texte: What do you do to avoid the noise and traffic?
questions.reponse: The person might answer: 'I go to parks or stay indoors when it's too noisy.'

questions.texte: Why do you think quiet places are important for relaxation?
questions.reponse: The person might answer: 'Quiet places help me think clearly and reduce stress.'

enonce.texte: Read the following open questions and write a 2-3 sentence response for each.

questions.texte: What are your hobbies and why do you enjoy them?
questions.reponse: I enjoy reading because it helps me relax and learn new things. I also like playing football because it keeps me fit and is fun.

questions.texte: How do you usually spend your weekends?
questions.reponse: I usually spend my weekends with my family. We often go to the market or visit friends. On Sundays, I like to rest and watch movies.

questions.texte: What do you think are the most important qualities in a friend?
questions.reponse: I think honesty and loyalty are the most important qualities in a friend. A good friend should also be supportive and kind.

enonce.texte:
You will participate in a group discussion on the topic:

'Should students be allowed to use smartphones in school?'

Write a script for the conversation. Include:

  • At least 5 questions from different speakers
  • At least 5 responses (agreeing, disagreeing, asking for clarification)
  • Use vocabulary from the lesson

questions.texte: Write a script of the discussion.
questions.reponse: Example: Speaker 1: 'I think students should be allowed to use smartphones in school because they can help with research.' Speaker 2: 'I disagree. I think phones are a distraction in class.' Speaker 1: 'But we can use them responsibly, can't we?' Speaker 3: 'I agree with Speaker 1. We can use phones for educational purposes.' Speaker 2: 'I understand, but not everyone can control themselves.' Speaker 1: 'That's true, but maybe we can have rules.' Speaker 3: 'I agree that rules are necessary. But we also need to be trusted.' Speaker 2: 'I'm not sure. I think it's better to keep phones away.' Speaker 1: 'What if we only use them for group activities?' Speaker 3: 'That sounds like a good compromise.'
